newsitem.title: USA: Modest buying bolsters U.S. mortgage-backeds.
newsitem.headline: Modest buying bolsters U.S. mortgage-backeds.

text.p: Light buying helped to bolster the price of U.S. mortgage-backed securities for the third straight trading session, and yield spreads to Treasuries were a tad tighter in late trade on Friday, traders said.

"There was some pretty good buying today, and mortgages held in pretty well for most of the day," said one Ginnie trader. He said he saw buying across the board with particular interest in Ginnie Mae paper.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent issues were up 14/32 at 99-21/32, yielding 97 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was up 13/32 at 99-21/32, and Freddie Mac issues were up 11/32 at 99-25/32.
The five-year note was up 11/32 at 6.51 percent, while the 10-year note was up 18/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
A mortgage analyst said Ginnie Mae current coupon spreads had tightened about two basis points over the week but should widen in the near future.
Cynthia Rivera, a mortgage research analyst at BZW Securities Inc, said Ginnie paper had reached the expensive end of its trading range.

"With the direction of the market going forward and volatility going into next week, spreads could widen on mortgages and current coupons by several basis points off their tights (yield spreads to Treasures)," she said.
Market participants are expected to remain sidelined until the the employment report slated for release on Friday, she said.
Economists in a Reuters poll forecast payrolls rose 221,000 in May, up from a 142,000 increase the previous month. They projected the unemployment rate climbed to 5.0 percent from 4.9 percent.
